transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

It may be worth fixing, but not until the airway is ruled out. A Henry that has lost suction and developed a rattly growl can be restricted by a blockage in the hose, tubes, floor tool or inlet; that makes the motor labour and sound rough even with a fresh bag and filter. With it unplugged, separate those parts and look straight through them, including the floor-tool neck—remove any debris you find. If everything is clear and it still growls with weak suction when used briefly with just the bare hose, a worn motor bearing, brushes or fan becomes the likely cause; on a 12-year-old machine, get a repair quote first, as motor work is only worthwhile if the cost is modest compared with a replacement.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
Thank you. I've checked the hose by dropping a coin through it and it goes straight through, so that seems clear. Suction is weak at both the hose end and the head. What should I try next?

The useful next test is at the machine itself, as that separates an internal airflow problem from a tired motor. Switch it off and unplug it, remove the hose, open the top and check the bag collar is fully seated and that there is no debris visible in the inlet just behind it; do not reach further in with tools. Then close it up and run it only briefly with the hose removed: is the suction at the bare inlet strong, or still weak, and is the rattly growl still present? If it is weak and rough even there, a worn motor bearing/brushes or damaged fan is the leading cause; that is engineer repair territory, and on a 12-year-old Henry it is worth obtaining a quote before authorising motor work.

Thank you. I'm afraid I'm not sure about the bag collar, but I fitted a genuine bag and a new cloth filter last week, both correctly. Should I run it with the hose off as you describe? It does get a hot electrical smell after about five minutes, and I've seen sparks flickering through the grille on top.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. I can't guide testing with the power on — that needs a qualified engineer. Any check I suggest is done with it switched off and unplugged. No — do not run it with the hose off, or use it again. A hot electrical smell together with visible sparking and the rough growl points strongly to a failing motor, commonly worn carbon brushes/commutator or a bearing/armature fault; an internal fan problem is another possibility. The clear hose and correctly fitted new bag and filter make a simple external blockage less likely. It needs a qualified vacuum-repair engineer to inspect the motor and internal airway with the machine isolated.
